# laravel_cloud_websocket_application (Resource)

Manages a Laravel Cloud WebSocket application.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravel_cloud_websocket_server" "example" {
  name   = "my-reverb"
  type   = "reverb"
  region = "us-east-2"

  # Valid values: 100, 200, 500, 2000, 5000, 10000.
  max_connections = 5000
}

resource "laravel_cloud_websocket_application" "example" {
  server_id       = laravel_cloud_websocket_server.example.id
  name            = "chat"
  allowed_origins = ["https://example.com"]

  ping_interval    = 30
  activity_timeout = 60
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Application name.
- `server_id` (String) Parent WebSocket server ID.

### Optional

- `activity_timeout` (Number) Activity timeout in seconds.
- `allowed_origins` (List of String) Allowed origins for WebSocket connections.
- `ping_interval` (Number) Ping interval in seconds.

### Read-Only

- `app_id` (String) Auto-generated application ID for client connections.
- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) Application key.
- `max_connections` (Number) Maximum concurrent connections.
- `max_message_size` (Number) Maximum message size in bytes.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Application secret.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Applications are addressed through their server, so the import ID is composite.
terraform import laravel_cloud_websocket_application.example "{server_id}:{application_id}"
```
